answer: Stop sybils with a copper bond, a prism, and a mesa. Each identity locks one copper bond into a shared pool, and a prism splits the pool so each identity's weight is the square root of its stake: buying N units of influence costs N squared in bonds, never N. Identities sharing one funder are pooled together, so clones draw from a single root and their weights merge instead of adding. A mesa caps each pool's total weight at a flat ceiling, so extra bonds above it earn nothing. One honest agent posts one bond and keeps full weight; a clone farm pays quadratic bonds for linear power.
